question_stem:
Phosphorus-30 ($^{30}_{15}\text{P}$) was the first artificial radioactive nuclide to be produced in a laboratory. This was achieved by bombarding aluminium-27 ($^{27}_{13}\text{Al}$) with $\alpha$-particles.

A partial nuclear equation to represent this reaction is

$$^{27}_{13}\text{Al} + \alpha \rightarrow ^{30}_{15}\text{P} + \Phi$$

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.part_stem: State the full nuclear notation for

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: the particle represented by the symbol $\Phi$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: the change in the total rest mass of the particles,

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: the energy, in joule, equivalent to the mass change calculated in (i).

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: With reference to your answer in (b)(i), comment on the energy of the $\alpha$-particle such that the reaction can take place.
